description: A thin bladed knife with a broad flat edge, held nearly flush against a hard surface to shave leather down to the wanted thickness. It cuts by means of a fine burr raised on the underside, giving close control over how much skin is removed. Cockerell names the French paring knife as a distinct binder's tool for leather, indexed separately from the general sharp knife used to pare paper.
name: French paring knife

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (D. Appleton, 1901), Internet Archive
